body: Auditor exits and delayed audited results preceded or accompanied many collapses: Reliance Capital & Reliance Home Finance (PwC resigned 2019 citing unresolved concerns), Byju's (Deloitte Jun 2023, BDO Sep 2024; FY21 accounts ~18 months late), Ricoh India (Q2FY16 results delayed after auditor queries), Jet Airways (Q1FY19 results deferred Aug 2018), Wirecard (KPMG special audit could not verify; EY refused 2019 sign-off), Credit Suisse (material weaknesses Mar 2023), Gensol/Brightcom (already in memory). In India, after the 2018-19 wave of mid-term auditor resignations, SEBI (Oct 2019) required auditors who resign to complete the quarter's limited review and disclose detailed reasons, which are filed on exchanges -- read them. Rules: (1) mid-term resignation with stated concerns (information not provided, fund diversion, going concern) = exit; (2) 'pre-occupation' or fee-related reasons from a large firm replaced by a tiny firm = strong flag; (3) delayed results beyond the regulatory deadline, or repeated qualified opinions/emphasis of matter on related-party balances = flag; (4) CFO resignation within months of auditor change compounds the signal. Auditor sign-off is weak evidence of honesty (Satyam/PwC, Wirecard/EY), but auditor exit is strong evidence of trouble.

data.rule: mid-term auditor exit with concerns = sell; big-to-tiny auditor switch = flag

title: Auditor resignation / delayed accounts as a disqualifier
